items.title: Designing Clinical Research (Browner, Newman, Cummings, Grady et al.; the 'Hulley' book), 5th ed. 2022
items.why: The best single book on turning a question into a feasible study: designs, sample size, measurement, ethics.

items.title: How to Read a Paper (Greenhalgh), 7th ed.
items.why: Short, readable appraisal of every design. Reading papers like a reviewer makes you write like one.

items.title: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions, v6.5 (2024)
items.why: The rulebook for SR methods. Cite it in every SR methods section.

items.title: Doing Meta-Analysis with R (Harrer, Cuijpers, Furukawa, Ebert)
items.why: Step-by-step R code for pooling, heterogeneity, subgroups, NMA and publication bias.

items.title: Medical Statistics at a Glance (Petrie & Sabin), 4th ed. 2019
items.why: Two-page spreads on each test. Ideal companion when choosing an analysis or answering a stats reviewer.

items.title: How to Write a Lot (Silvia), 2nd ed. 2019
items.why: The habit book: schedule writing like a theatre list and stop waiting for free weekends.

items.title: Writing Your Journal Article in Twelve Weeks (Belcher), 2nd ed. 2019
items.why: A week-by-week workbook to take a draft to submission. Good for unsticking a stalled paper. ISBN 9780226499918.

items.title: R for Health Data Science / HealthyR (Harrison & Pius)
items.why: Written by surgeons for surgeons; finalfit tables and regression the way ortho journals want them.

items.title: R for Data Science, 2nd ed. (Wickham, Cetinkaya-Rundel, Grolemund)
items.why: The tidyverse foundation for cleaning and plotting.

items.title: Flexible Imputation of Missing Data, 2nd ed. (van Buuren)
items.why: The reference for multiple imputation with mice.

items.title: Citing Medicine, 2nd ed. (NLM)
items.why: Every Vancouver reference format you will ever need.

items.title: NIHR Learn (GCP, Associate PI, informed consent, research skills)
items.why: GCP certificate for sponsors and CTUs; Associate PI scheme modules.

items.title: Cochrane Interactive Learning
items.cost: Paid, with free access for some groups (check eligibility via Cochrane help pages)
items.why: Module-by-module SR training; good onboarding for your second reviewers.

items.title: NOTP Surgical Research Course (NDORMS/SITU, endorsed by the four surgical Royal Colleges)
items.why: National online research-methods course for UK surgical trainees, with certificate. Check LED access via the PGVLE.

items.title: BOASTiC: Bristol, Oxford and Aberdeen Surgical Trials intervention course 2026
items.why: Hands-on course for designing surgical trials.

items.title: RCSEd: Clinical Research Methodology in a Nutshell
items.why: Royal College short course covering the research basics.

items.title: Coursera / Johns Hopkins: Design and Interpretation of Clinical Trials
items.why: Solid trial design grounding before you act as site PI or co-applicant.

items.title: NHS-R Community (training, webinars, Slack)
items.why: NHS-flavoured R training and a friendly Slack for code help.

items.title: Global Health Training Centre (The Global Health Network)
items.why: Free short e-learning on GCP, research ethics, data management and trial methods.
items.url_check: stable official URL; not re-checked today

items.title: OpenLearn (Open University) free health and research courses
items.why: Short introductory courses; useful for students joining your team.
items.url_check: stable official URL; not re-checked today

items.title: Happy Git and GitHub for the useR (Bryan)
items.why: Version control for your analysis code (code only, never patient data).

items.title: EQUATOR Network
items.why: Every reporting guideline in one place. Download the checklist at protocol stage.

items.title: CEBM: OCEBM Levels of Evidence
items.why: The levels table behind the evidence pyramid, with notes on grading up and down.

items.title: Students 4 Best Evidence (S4BE, Cochrane)
items.why: Short blogs on EBM concepts; great for training students and FY doctors on your team.

items.title: PRISMA statement site (checklists, flow diagrams)
items.why: PRISMA 2020 checklist and flow templates.

items.title: PROSPERO
items.why: Register SRs before screening.

items.title: OSF Registries
items.why: Register scoping reviews and observational studies; host code and data with a DOI.

items.title: HRA decision tools
items.why: The first click for every project with patients or staff.

items.title: BJJ instructions for authors
items.why: Word, author and figure limits plus the preprint ban.

items.title: Clarivate Master Journal List
items.why: Check Web of Science indexing (SCIE/ESCI) for ST3.

items.title: NLM Catalog
items.why: MEDLINE status and journal abbreviations.

items.title: Orthobullets
items.why: Its research/biostatistics topics and evidence summaries are quick refreshers before interviews and journal clubs.

items.title: riskofbias.info (RoB 2, ROBINS-I V2, ROBINS-E)
items.why: Official risk-of-bias tools and guidance.

items.title: GRADEpro GDT
items.why: Builds Summary of Findings tables.

items.title: Rayyan
items.why: Blind dual screening for SRs.

items.title: Zotero + Better BibTeX
items.why: Reference management and stable citation keys for Quarto/R.

items.title: BOA research hub and BOTA
items.why: UK T&O research news, JLA priorities, trainee collaboratives.

items.title: BJJ Podcasts (Bone & Joint Publishing)
items.why: Authors explain their BJJ papers; good for hearing how a study was framed and defended.

items.title: JAMAevidence: JAMA Guide to Statistics and Methods
items.why: 15-minute episodes, each on one statistical method used in a real trial.

items.title: StatQuest with Josh Starmer
items.why: Clear visual explanations of regression, p-values, ROC curves and more.
items.url_check: stable official URL; not re-checked today

items.title: Cochrane Training (webinars and learning live)
items.why: Recorded methods webinars on SR topics.
items.url_check: stable official URL; not re-checked today

items.title: North West Orthopaedic Research Collaborative
items.why: Your regional trainee collaborative: multicentre data and named roles.

items.title: Shut Up & Write (Health Professions Education Research Writing Group)
items.why: Online accountability writing sessions.

items.title: X/Twitter research communities (#MedTwitter, #OrthoTwitter, #EvidenceSynthesis, @EQUATORNetwork, @Cochrane)
items.why: Fast news on guidelines, methods and calls for collaborators. Treat claims as leads, not evidence.
items.url_check: stable official URL; not re-checked today
